transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-04-27 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 58m
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Evelyn (Shearwater Head ML), Rahul (CTO), Tara (Infra)

Summary (auto): quick budget-first discovery to map hosted vs dedicated vs private economics. Customer wants a pilot budget for recommendation replies and an evaluation of batching/caching levers. SOC2/KMS and VPC constraints discussed.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining — quick run of agenda, we want to map your budget and per-token target and then sketch hosting options and next steps
00:34 Evelyn Park: yeah thanks, we are trying to model the economics before committing to infra. two use cases — chat assistant with about 5k avg tokens/session and a shorter summarization pipeline at ~400 tokens. rough daily active sessions 8k for chat, 50k for summary.
01:10 Rahul Singh: also need to say we have strict residency, most PII stays in our VPC. thinking private or dedicated but want an apples-to-apples cost comp with hosted.
01:35 Carlos Ruiz: got it. a couple clarifying Qs — are those 5k tokens full roundtrip or input-only? and do you expect streaming requirements?
01:50 Evelyn Park: 5k is mostly output, input is typically 500 tokens. streaming is nice for UX but not required for the first pilot.
02:18 Tara Mendez: network wise we can't punch out to public endpoints for model payloads containing certain PD fields, so if hosted path is used we need private connectivity or token redaction.
02:40 Maya Chen: totally, we can do VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud. For hosted we also offer private placement (dedicated networking) — but that shifts the pricing model.
03:05 Carlos Ruiz: quick note on levers — per-token price is one factor, another is batching (how many concurrent requests you can group) and prefix/KV cache which reduces repeated decoding cost for similar prompts. those substantially change unit economics.
03:28 Rahul Singh: can you give ballpark numbers for hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved capacity?
03:40 Maya Chen: high level: hosted per-token covers compute + infra + managed ops; for models with long outputs we sometimes see $0.0006–$0.002 per token depending on model family and sequence length. Dedicated moves to a committed monthly for GPUs plus a smaller per-token compute charge; for high volume (>500k–1M tokens/day) dedicated typically becomes cheaper.
04:10 Evelyn Park: that's a wide range, any example for a 5k-output chat?
04:20 Carlos Ruiz: example sketch — for a 5k average output hosted might be in the higher bracket due to compute time; but if you can batch short windows or use prefix caching for repeated system prompt/context we can reduce effective tokens billed or amortized compute by 20–40%. also quantization/8-bit models can cut GPU runtime cost but we need to validate quality.
05:05 Tara Mendez: when you say caching, do you cache user-specific KV state or only public prefixes? we can't cache PII across shared caches.
05:20 Carlos Ruiz: good point — we support both. prefix cache for common system prompts is safe; KV cache for long-running conversations is per-customer ephemeral and can be kept inside your VPC if using Private. caching policy is configurable.
05:45 Rahul Singh: how do rollouts/fallbacks work if a dedicated pool is saturated?
05:52 Maya Chen: policy router — we can failover to a hosted pool or a smaller model variant automatically, with configurable SLO for latency and cost. for enterprise pilots we usually set a burst policy to prevent dropped requests.
06:15 Evelyn Park: what about audit logs and key management? must tie into our KMS and have encrypted logs for compliance.
06:28 Maya Chen: Redwood Private and Dedicated both integrate with customer KMS/HSM and produce audit logs. Hosted can also integrate via customer-managed keys for model payload encryption at rest. We'll include the SOC2 extract in follow-ups.
06:50 Carlos Ruiz: could we walk through a quick back-of-envelope for 1M tokens/day chat (mix of 5k and 400 token calls)?
07:02 Rahul Singh: yes please, we need to present this to finance tomorrow as a sanity check.
07:12 Carlos Ruiz: if we assume 8k chat sessions/day * 5k output = 40M tokens, wait that's too high, sorry — let me recalc: if 8k sessions with 5k output that's 40M tokens — OK that scales. plus 50k summaries * 400 = 20M tokens, total 60M tokens/day. Is that your peak?
07:44 Evelyn Park: that's peak; our early pilot target is 1M tokens/day with growth. we wanted a pilot budget to explore 1M/day and a path to 10M.
07:58 Maya Chen: perfect. for 1M tokens/day hosted at $0.001/token (mid-range) that'd be $1k/day or ~$30k/month. Dedicated reserved capacity could be structured as a monthly commit that might be ~$12–18k/month plus variable. This is very model and batching dependent.
08:25 Tara Mendez: can you show the sensitivity to batching? like how much we save if average batch size goes from 2 to 8?
08:35 Carlos Ruiz: yes, batching reduces per-token GPU overhead. a rough rule: going from batch 2 to 8 can cut per-token runtime by ~20–40% for attention-heavy models, but it's sensitive to request length distribution. we'll run a quick sim for your traces.
09:05 Evelyn Park: is prefix caching effective if our prompts include dynamic customer context?
09:12 Carlos Ruiz: if you can split out static system instructions and common reference text into a prefix, that part can be cached, so subsequent traffic reuses that work. dynamic customer-specific parts can't be shared across users unless you want per-user caches (which we can keep inside Private mode).
09:40 Rahul Singh: any tradeoffs on latency for larger batches? our SLO for interactive chat is <600ms 95th percentile.
09:50 Carlos Ruiz: batching trades throughput for latency — for strict 600ms SLOs we often set small batching windows and rely more on prefix caching and model routing to lower-cost variants for non-critical requests. If you can tolerate 1–1.5s tail it opens more batching opportunities.
10:15 Maya Chen: also worth considering model selection; smaller / quantized models for common flows, full large models for high-value queries. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and model mix per route.
10:36 Tara Mendez: from infra side, if we go Dedicated in our cloud region, how much network egress vs internal?
10:45 Maya Chen: if Dedicated is in your VPC it's internal; hosted with PrivateLink still traverses secure private connectivity. We'll need a topology doc to validate egress.
11:05 Evelyn Park: security question: retention windows for logs and traces — can we specify retention = 30 days and then auto-delete?
11:15 Maya Chen: yes adjustable retention, plus audit exports. For Private we can route logs to your SIEM and control retention entirely.
11:30 Rahul Singh: one more procurement angle — our procurement likes predictable monthly cost not per-token spikes. how do you usually structure pilots to satisfy that?
11:45 Maya Chen: typical path: start hosted trial to validate model quality, then transition to a time-limited Dedicated pilot with a smaller monthly commit and cap on overage. We also offer burst pools to smooth spikes.
12:03 Tara Mendez: curious about fallback QoS — do you degrade gracefully if budget threshold hit?
12:10 Carlos Ruiz: yes you can configure tiered fallback: lower-cost model, reduced max tokens, or queue with synchronous failover; policies are per-route and can be automated.
12:35 Evelyn Park: ok we're trying to be pragmatic — give us three scenarios for 1M tokens/day pilot: hosted, dedicated small commit, and private (on-prem) sketch.
12:50 Maya Chen: we'll produce that. quick note: private on-prem introduces infra setup time (~4–8 weeks) and larger fixed costs. Dedicated commit is usually 4–12 week ramp. Hosted is fastest to validate.
13:18 Rahul Singh: any benchmarking we can run ourselves? we can provide traces and you run a short perf bench?
13:25 Carlos Ruiz: yes — best is you drop 3 days of traces and we run a bench using the same model family and sim traffic to show latency/burn under different batching/cache configs. we'll also show per-route cost delta.
13:50 Evelyn Park: transcription glitch: when you say "burn" do you mean token spend? we use burn informally internally yes.
13:57 Maya Chen: yes token burn = actual billed tokens/compute.
14:08 Tara Mendez: timeline-wise we need procurement sign-off within three weeks if pilot cost is < $50k.
14:18 Maya Chen: understood. we'll prioritize the hosted quick-start and cost sketch in the next 48–72 hours to meet your timeline.
14:40 Carlos Ruiz: small gotcha: quality regressions with quantized models can appear on long-context outputs — we'll include a short eval on your prompts.
15:05 Rahul Singh: great. any competitors or other vendors we should be aware of? we are also talking to XYZ vendor and internal ops.
15:18 Maya Chen: noted. we'll share a feature/price comparison and emphasize the inference routing and observability differences.
15:30 Evelyn Park: ok let's recap next steps — Redwood shares docs + cost sketches, Shearwater shares traces and prompts, follow-up meeting to review bench.
15:48 Maya Chen: perfect. Thanks everyone.
